A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ParaSpeechCaps study. Their main text, Tables 1–7, Figures 1–13 and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including material moved during reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluations of dataset quality, trained TTS models, compositional generation and ablations in Sections 4–5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–4 and the compositional and per-tag analyses in Figures 5 and 8.

M1.justification: The VoxSim-based intrinsic tagging, three-stage situational tagging pipeline, Parler-TTS training and classifier-free-guidance inference procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same source corpora, English-language coverage, 59-tag taxonomy and single-tag and compositional TTS tasks. The corrected abstract duration does not establish a change to the underlying dataset.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Parler-TTS, +LTTSR and +LTTSP,Exp,EARS as baselines. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the dataset ablations, compositional evaluation and guidance comparisons.

E3.justification: Splits, sampling procedures, metrics, training budgets and inference settings are retained. Section 5.1 newly states that the main test set contains 246 examples, but describes the same construction; this is additional disclosure rather than a reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: The embedding and pipeline-stage ablations, guidance ablation and per-tag intelligibility analysis are unchanged. The new bias limitation does not introduce a corresponding robustness test or systematic bias analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three human evaluation annotations per example and report MOS means with 95% confidence intervals. No repeated-run, seed, significance-testing or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The abstract corrects PSC-Base from 342 to 282 hours, agreeing with v1's introduction and conclusion. v2 also newly reports qualitative overrepresentation of female speakers for shrill and male speakers for guttural. Experimental scores in Tables 2–4 and Figures 5 and 8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The taxonomy, metric definitions and mathematical descriptions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs that are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract's quantitative contribution statement is corrected from 342 to 282 human-labelled hours, matching the existing body text. The central claims about 59 tags, automatic scaling, annotation quality and TTS improvements are otherwise unchanged.

C2.justification: A new Dataset biases limitation explains how tag correlations, particularly gender-associated styles, could be amplified during dataset construction and learned by models, restricting diverse style–speaker combinations. Existing language and evaluation-metric limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly discloses the main evaluation set's 246-example total. The acknowledgements also identify Empire AI computing resources. Existing implementation settings, appendix prompts, preprocessing instructions and release information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Sections 2.2 and 6 are unchanged. No new comparison with prior research or revised novelty relationship is introduced.

P1.justification: There are limited textual additions to the experimental setup, limitations and acknowledgements, plus the abstract correction. Most prose and the section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned: Figure 2 and Table 2 change columns, and Table 7 moves from PDF page 14 to 15. Appendix prompt blocks reflow and page-number footers disappear. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves an inconsistent abstract dataset size, discloses the evaluation sample count and adds a substantive demographic-bias limitation. These improve accuracy, transparency and qualification of the contribution. The gains are limited because the experimental results and appendix analyses remain unchanged, and the new bias observations are not quantified.
